About Veoneer Safety Systems:
 Veoneer exists to Protect Everyone in Every Crash. We design, manufacture, and sell the world's best automotive safety electronics.
Veoneer is a world leader, and almost every 4th car produced today has Veoneer's automotive safety electronics. Veoneer has delivered more than 1.1 billion electronic control units and crash sensors to car manufacturers globally.
The company is building on a heritage of 70 years of automotive safety development. Veoneer is owned by AIP, is headquartered in the U.S., and has approximately 2,383 employees in 11 countries.
 Position Summary:
 As a Cyber Security Engineer, you will contribute to both Product Security Incident Response (PSIRT) and Cyber Security Fuzz Testing, helping identify, analyse, test, and manage cybersecurity vulnerabilities affecting automotive embedded products throughout their lifecycle.
 What you'll do?
Monitor and identify potential cybersecurity vulnerabilities and events affecting automotive embedded products.
Triage and evaluate cybersecurity events and support vulnerability analysis and risk assessment.
Perform Cyber Security Fuzz Testing on automotive embedded ECUs and software.
Define and deploy fuzz-testing methods according to ISO 21434 and applicable Cyber Security standards.
Plan and execute fuzz-test activities using dedicated Cyber Security testing tools.
Analyze fuzz-test results, identify potential vulnerabilities, and document findings in Fuzz Test Reports.
Support engineering and project Cyber Security teams in analyzing identified vulnerabilities, test results, and potential weaknesses.
Contribute to vulnerability and cybersecurity incident management, including remediation of identified vulnerabilities.
Support appropriate communication and disclosure activities related to cybersecurity vulnerabilities and incidents.
Collaborate with international product development, engineering, and Cyber Security teams.
Contribute to the standardization and continuous improvement of Cyber Security testing and vulnerability-management methods.
 What you'll bring:
Degree in Electronics, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent.
Good understanding of embedded systems, software/hardware, and Cyber Security.
Experience in development or testing of embedded real-time systems.
Strong interest in automotive cybersecurity and vulnerability analysis.
Knowledge of ISO 21434 / automotive Cyber Security is an advantage.
Experience with fuzz-testing tools such as Defensics is a strong advantage.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to investigate technical issues and work collaboratively with engineering and Cyber Security teams.
Ability to work effectively in an international environment.
Advanced English and good communication skills.
Cyber Security certification is a plus.
